reviews.title: Unusable in Current State
reviews.text:
I have been using Acrobat Reader for years, possibly decades.  It has usually been a better-than-average app.

The last few versions, though, have been terrible.  Previous versions have been slow to open, but the latest version is interminably slow.

I keep all my documents on my iPad.  I have many files, of various sizes, from kbs, to numerous MBs.

My iPad is a 9th generation, running the current version of OS, and the most recent version of the app.

Doing anything causes the app to be inoperative for several, and often many, seconds, before it responds, to the point where even something as simple as renaming a document can take up to two minutes to complete.

I cannot delete and reinstall the app, in what I suspect would be a futile attempt to improve 
performance as, as previously stated, all my documents are on my iPad, and will be deleted with the app.

Also, I cannot move my documents to the cloud, so they will survive deleting the app, as app responsiveness is that slow, that transferring each file, individually, will drive me insane.  I tried to transfer five files to the cloud this evening, four small, and one around 10MB (not that big).  It took 45 minutes just to transfer these five files, which, quite frankly, is ludicrous.

reviews.title: Lock-in. Quality-out.
reviews.text:
Adobe's current business model prioritizes ecosystem lock-in over user experience, particularly regarding cross-platform file management and interface transparency.

Technical Critiques and Bad Faith Practices

• Dark Patterns in Cloud Integration: The software intentionally complicates the use of third-party storage like Google Drive by defaulting to Adobe Cloud prompts, forcing users into a proprietary ecosystem even when they have already paid for other services.

• Feature Obfuscation: Essential tools like page bookmarks, which are standard in digital reading, are frequently hidden or removed from main toolbars in favor of subscription-based editing features.

• Retention through Friction: Instead of fostering loyalty through superior performance, Adobe creates "software friction" where native OS behaviors (like the standard Windows File Explorer) are suppressed to prioritize Adobe's own rental-based services.

• Inconsistent iPad Implementation: The iPad application lacks the robust "restore last view" settings found in the desktop version, compelling users to manually manage reading progress unless they use Adobe’s cloud-syncing services.
